facts.text: OT2MotionController is a thin wrapper around the existing Opentrons driver classes; it does not reimplement the low-level serial communication
The controller serializes hardware calls on one asyncio.Lock, wrapped in a _TimedLock with lock_timeout_s, because the SmoothieDriver has a single serial connection
stop() is documented as an emergency stop that halts all motion: it acquires that lock and then calls SmoothieDriver.hard_halt(); the clone does not implement hard_halt itself
move(target, speed=None) awaits SmoothieDriver.move while it holds the lock; target maps axes to positions and speed is in mm/sec
move_through documents its targets as axis letters mapped to absolute mm and its speeds in mm/sec

home(axes) holds the lock while it homes the gantry and mount axes together and then each plunger axis B/C on its own at the attached pipette's run current or a safe default, because the bare driver would home a plunger at the 0.05 A idle current, which lacks the torque to reach the endstop
get_position() calls SmoothieDriver.update_position while it holds the lock and returns the updated cached position
aspirate moves the plunger axis up from its cached position by volume_ul / ul_per_mm at flow_rate_ul_s / ul_per_mm mm/s while it holds the lock; the caller must first place the plunger at its bottom
dispense moves the plunger axis down from its cached position by volume_ul / ul_per_mm at flow_rate_ul_s / ul_per_mm mm/s while it holds the lock
reset_from_error() clears the alarm lock with M999 and smoothie_reset() performs a full GPIO reset of the Smoothie, each while holding the lock

After reset_from_error or smoothie_reset the homed flags are all false and the operator must re-home before moving; smoothie_reset is the more drastic GPIO pulse and reset_from_error is preferred for alarm recovery
The clone's plan states that no reliable alarm-state signal is available without modifying the driver and that all-false homed flags cannot be told apart from a robot not homed since boot
read_pipette_model(mount) and read_pipette_id(mount) read the pipette EEPROM while holding the lock and return an empty string when nothing is read (no pipette attached, or an unreadable id)

set_button_light sets the RGB front-button LED, set_rail_lights switches the deck rail lights, get_button_light returns an (r, g, b) tuple, get_rail_lights a bool, and read_button and read_door_switch return the front-button and door-switch states
get_serial_number reads /var/serial and returns an empty string when it is unavailable
get_firmware_version queries the Smoothie firmware version
is_simulating reports the SmoothieDriver.simulating flag
build(port, simulate=False) sets up the GPIO character device and builds a _RaisingSmoothieDriver on the serial port; simulate=True builds a simulating GPIO and a SmoothieDriver without a connection

_RaisingSmoothieDriver raises SmoothieAlarm on the first alarm reply while a hard halt is set (and clears it) and SmoothieError on an error reply then; outside a hard halt it raises SmoothieError on every alarm or error reply, including the 'alarm lock' and 'after halt you should home' replies that the upstream driver swallows
A comment in move_through states that after a mid-line alarm the alarm path inside _send_command has already reset and homed

The OT-2 axes are X, Y, Z, A, B and C: X is the gantry, Y moves toward the front window when negative, Z/A are the left/right mount vertical axes and B/C the left/right plungers; each axis has its limit switch at its positive end

A feature-layer comment states that Opentrons provides no fixed floor for the Z/A mount axes (HOMED_POSITION defines only the top) and that a replayed robot-server request executed a machine position below 0 (-21.44 mm) without error
The clone's feature layer states that the physical limit switches are the real safety boundary for Z/A and that no synthetic software floor is enforced there; the X/Y 0.0 floor is marked untested
The feature layer's _check_bounds refuses a position outside the controller's axis_bounds maximum or the feature's lower limit for the axis
The feature layer's emergency_stop is documented to immediately halt all motion; it calls the controller stop and returns 'Emergency stop executed. Re-home required before resuming.'
The upstream simulation tests state that in simulation emergency_stop sets an internal flag only, with no actual halt, and that pause and resume do nothing
The module imports opentrons.drivers.smoothie_drivers.driver_3_0.SmoothieDriver; the hard-halt and serial details are in that dependency and are not shown in the clone
The clone depends on opentrons 8.8.1 below Python 3.12 and on opentrons 9.0.0 from Python 3.12

safe_state.description: OT2MotionController.stop() has returned: it called SmoothieDriver.hard_halt() (Opentrons code outside the clone) once the controller lock was free, which a running move or home releases only when its cancellation ends it; nothing senses standstill. The driver then sends no Smoothie command except the re-enable (M999 and a full home of all six axes): motion actions are refused PRECONDITION_UNMET and the position, firmware and pipette reads are absent until it completes
